crime.value: Murder by bludgeoning. George Hobday killed with head battered in under a hedge. Central question: Did Harry Evitt's alibi—a timed telephone call to the exchange and clock manipulation—successfully conceal his guilt?
crime.quote: At the time when his body was discovered, under a hedge and with his head battered in, he had been dead for at least an hour.

victim.value: George Hobday, business partner of Harry Evitt in the firm Hobday and Hobday (auctioneers and estate agents). Killable because he discovered financial irregularities—Evitt embezzling or misappropriating company money.
victim.quote: You've had it ready for a long time, in case George ever found out about the money.

closed_world.value: A rural English village with limited transport (train arrivals on schedule, footpaths across fields, short windows of movement). The Evitts' house and surrounding properties form the investigative perimeter.
closed_world.quote: The short cut across the fields...he needed only five minutes to reach the Evitts' house.

culprit_and_motive.value: Harry Evitt murdered George Hobday to prevent discovery of embezzlement or financial crime. Motive: self-preservation and concealment of theft from the business partnership.
culprit_and_motive.quote: You've had it ready, yet you never told me...I've had it ready in case George ever found out about the money.

resolution.value: Inspector Tewson deduces that Rina Evitt deliberately disrupted Minnie Hobday's watch using a magnetic pencil from the telephone pad during bridge. The watch's erratic behavior (gaining time unpredictably) exposed the alibi as constructed.
resolution.quote: If you keep on tapping a watch with a quite powerful magnet, you can make it go very wrong indeed...you can't tell if it'll go fast or slow or stop altogether.

investigator.value: Detective Inspector Ronald Tewson, official police investigator. A methodical, anger-driven detective suspicious of the Evitts' convenient clock and phone alibi from the start.
investigator.quote: Detective Inspector Ronald Tewson was very interested in Minnie's watch...the unwarranted conclusion to which he jumped was that George Hobday had been murdered by his partner, Harry Evitt.
